learning_outcomes: Understand financial control as a pattern of coercive behaviour.
Recognise financial control tactics in parenting, co-parenting, and family systems.
Identify behavioural and structural signs of economic abuse.
Interpret the impact of financial control on children and caregivers.
Apply safe, supportive responses and basic safety planning around money.

lesson_content.definition: Financial control tactics are patterns of behaviour that restrict, manipulate, or dominate another person’s access to money, resources, and economic independence.

core_components.name: Conditional Provision
examples: Only providing money as a reward for compliance
Making basic needs dependent on obedience

core_components.name: Sabotage of Income
examples: Creating crises that cause job loss

core_components.name: Debt & Financial Risk Imposition
examples: Forcing loans or credit in the victim’s name
Refusing to contribute to shared responsibilities

core_components.name: Child-Linked Financial Control
examples: Controlling school, activity, or medical costs to gain power

child_specific_impacts: Inconsistent access to food, clothing, and essentials
Stress about money and basic needs
Feeling responsible for adult financial problems
Reduced participation in school and activities
Long-term anxiety about security and stability
parent_specific_impacts: Limited ability to plan for safety or future

video_lesson.title: Understanding Financial Control Tactics
script: Financial control is a powerful form of coercive behaviour that limits a person’s autonomy and safety.
It can look like restricted access to money, sabotaged income, or using children’s expenses as leverage.
Over time, financial control traps families in instability and makes it harder to leave unsafe situations.
Recognising these tactics early helps parents protect themselves and their children, and seek support safely.

activities.description: Sort behaviours into correct financial control categories.
Identify financial control patterns and explain likely impacts.

scenarios.text: A parent refuses to pay for school excursions unless the other parent follows their demands.
A partner insists on handling all money and never shares account details.

fill_in_the_blank.question: Financial control tactics restrict a person’s access to ________ and resources.
Sabotaging employment is a form of ________ of income.
Using child-related expenses as leverage is ________-linked financial control.
Economic dependence reduces a person’s ________ to leave unsafe situations.
Running up debt in another person’s name is a ________ risk tactic.

multiple_choice.question: Which behaviour is an example of financial control?
options: Blocking access to shared bank accounts
multiple_choice.answer: Blocking access to shared bank accounts

multiple_choice.question: Which behaviour is an example of sabotage of income?

true_false.question: Financial control can occur even when there is no physical violence.
Children are never affected by financial control tactics.

short_answer.question: Name two impacts of financial control on children.
Why is financial control harmful even when basic needs are sometimes met?

scenario_questions.question: A partner runs up debt in the other’s name without consent. Which category does this belong to?
A parent only pays for school supplies when the other parent complies with demands. Which category does this belong to?

competency_check: Identify financial control tactics across family contexts
Explain economic, emotional, and developmental impacts
Apply safe, supportive responses and basic safety planning
Recognise early warning signs of economic abuse
extensions: Teaching Children Basic Financial Safety Concepts
